clue.text: Incentive for exceeding one's duty?

parts.note: doing more than your duty here means working extra hours, and the incentive is the extra wages paid for them

explanation.definitionFit: Extra wages for hours worked beyond the normal shift reward going past what the job requires.

clue.text: Mood in which gold may be found?

definitions.text: in which gold may be found?

explanation.definitionFit: A vein is a mood or humour (in a merry vein), and also a seam of ore in rock where gold is mined.

clue.text: A knot the navigator should avoid

explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a square knot, and also a ridge of rock just under the sea that sailors steer clear of.

clue.text: Designs 10 isn't worried about

indicators.note: worried about means knocked around and disturbed, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: the number ten written as a word

explanation.surface: A designer shrugs off concern for some project numbered ten.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' here is the plain number ten, not a reference to the clue at 10 across; 'worried about' rearranges TEN with ISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Intents are purposes or aims, just as designs can mean plans or intentions.

clue.text: Eagle-eyed overseas winger

parts.note: a sharp-sighted bird of prey that flies over the sea, read as a description of a sea eagle rather than a keen-eyed footballer

explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a bird that hunts over coastal waters.

clue.text: Extremely high tar!

parts.note: tar is slang for a sailor, so an extremely high one is a sailor of the top naval rank, not a strong cigarette

explanation.definitionFit: A naval officer of the highest rank is the most senior sailor of all.

clue.text: Confection made with breadfruit?

parts.note: breadfruit is read as bread with fruit in it, a loaf dotted with dried berries, not the tropical tree

explanation.definitionFit: A sweet bake of dough studded with small dried grapes is exactly bread containing fruit.

clue.text: Individually designed watch cases

parts.note: watch means a guard on duty, and the cases are the one-person shelters a guard stands in, not boxes for a wristwatch

explanation.definitionFit: Small shelters for a single guard keeping watch are each built for one occupant.

clue.text: Revised clue that is decidedly fishy

indicators.note: revised means altered and rewritten, so the word clue is rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter's rewritten clue is now highly suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fishy' looks like 'suspect', but the definition means a thing that really is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The luce is an old name for the pike, a freshwater fish.

clue.text: Say what you want to christen the child

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an invitation to state your choice of drink or reward, and literally means bestowing a title on a baby.

clue.text: Go jogging and turn to right

indicators.note: turn means the letters are turned round and read backwards

explanation.surface: Advice to a runner to set off and take a right-hand turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses TO plus RT (TORT) to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trot is a gentle run, so going at one is like jogging.

clue.text: What can give Nepal better justice?

parts.note: a re-forming of the letters of the word penal gives the country name Nepal

explanation.surface: A question about improving the legal system of a Himalayan kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as wordplay says: rearrange PENAL, and you get NEPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvement of prisons and punishment is meant to make the justice system fairer.

clue.text: Wildly cheers great set of divine Greek charmers

indicators.note: wildly means in a disorderly way, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A crowd cheers loudly for a lovely group of goddesses.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth three sister goddesses personified beauty, charm and joy.

clue.text: Strongly urges increased productivity.

parts.note: read as a manager pressing staff to produce more, the whole clue is an example of earnest urging

explanation.definitionFit: To press someone earnestly to act, as a boss might push for more output.

clue.text: Type of guided missile now obsolete

definitions.text: Type of guided missile now obsolete

parts.words: Type of guided missile now obsolete
parts.note: guided missile suggests a modern rocket, but the clue means an old hand-thrown weapon aimed by the thrower

explanation.definitionFit: A long pointed shaft hurled by hand is an ancient weapon no longer used in war.

clue.text: Post free?

parts.note: post means a job, so a free one is a position nobody holds, not postage paid

explanation.definitionFit: An unfilled job opening is a position waiting for someone to take it.

clue.text: A girl with a face like a fiddle!

definitions.text: A girl with a face like a fiddle!

parts.words: A girl with a face like a fiddle!
parts.note: a girl's first name that is also the name of a stringed instrument resembling a violin

explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's name and also the alto member of the violin family.

clue.text: Inflict damage on unwanted produce of mine

explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something, and also the waste rock dug out of a mine and piled in heaps.

clue.text: Positively have something to say

parts.note: to state a thing positively is to declare it as true with confidence

explanation.definitionFit: To assert or affirm something firmly.

clue.text: 16 down's a lot different

indicators.note: different means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that the girl at 16 down is much changed.
explanation.walkthrough: The viola at 16 down is called the alto in French and in some orchestral usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The viola plays in the middle register and is named the alto in French.

clue.text: It isn't true it comes to a moral conclusion

definitions.text: It isn't true it comes to a moral conclusion

parts.words: It isn't true it comes to a moral conclusion
parts.note: a made-up story that ends with a lesson, like Aesop's tales

explanation.definitionFit: A short invented tale, often with animals, that closes with a lesson.

clue.text: What soldiers do when they leave a dossier available for inspection?

definitions.text: What soldiers do when they leave

explanation.definitionFit: Troops march away in a line, and a folder of documents is set out for people to see.

clue.text: Ancient city in which sheep stray before us

indicators.note: before places the shuffled sheep ahead of the word us
sheep that stray wander off, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: Flocks wander around an old town ahead of our arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a flock wandering, but 'stray' is the anagram signal and 'before' sets that scramble ahead of the final two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a great Greek city in Asia Minor, now ruins in Turkey.

clue.text: Horseplay just after kit-inspection at Aldershot?

indicators.note: after puts the word for just in second place

parts.note: a rag is a boisterous student or barracks prank
just means fair, as in a fair decision

explanation.surface: Soldiers mess about once their equipment has been checked.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldershot is a big British Army garrison town; a rag-fair is old army slang for a kit inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: In old soldiers' slang the laying out of kit for inspection was compared to a market of old clothes.

clue.text: Calm primate swallowing vegetarian fare

indicators.note: swallowing means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: an ape is a primate
peas are vegetables, meat-free food

explanation.surface: A gorilla keeps quiet while eating its greens.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify someone is to soothe them.

clue.text: Youngster brought up in a stable environment

definitions.text: Youngster brought up in a stable environment

parts.words: Youngster brought up in a stable environment
parts.note: a stable environment sounds like a secure home, but means a horse's stall where a young animal grows up

explanation.definitionFit: A young horse is raised in a stable.

clue.text: A brother of 20 across?

parts.note: the title used for the animals of Uncle Remus tales, a dialect word for brother, as in the tale of the rabbit

explanation.definitionFit: In the Uncle Remus stories the dialect title for brother is given to the animal heroes such as the rabbit.

clue.text: Tall pine

explanation.definitionFit: Long can mean of great height, and to long is to yearn for something.

clue.text: Dead form of Scandinavian literature

indicators.note: form as a verb means shape anew, so the letters of dead are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that an old Nordic literary genre is extinct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' looks like a noun meaning 'type', but it is the anagram signal on DEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddas are medieval Icelandic collections of Norse myth and poetry.

clue.text: Writes and agrees

explanation.definitionFit: To exchange letters with someone, and also to match or tally.

clue.text: Ruminant returns for a marsh plant

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a deer is a cud-chewing animal

explanation.surface: A grazing animal comes back to feed on wetland vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall grass growing in wet ground is a typical wetland plant.

clue.text: A warning that trouble is expected

definitions.text: A warning that trouble is expected

parts.words: A warning that trouble is expected
parts.note: trouble here is bad weather at sea, and the warning is a flag or cone hoisted at ports

explanation.definitionFit: A cone or flag raised at harbours warned sailors of gales on the way.
